chunks: That was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Hajj is of three types: Ifrad, Qiran, and Tamattu' (with Umrah to Hajj). And the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) commanded with it, and the virtue is in it, so we do not command the people except with it.

key_terms.إِقْرَانٌ: Qiran: A form of Hajj where one combines Hajj and Umrah together in one Ihram.
key_terms.تَمَتُّعٌ: Tamattu': A form of Hajj where one performs Umrah first, releases from Ihram, and then performs Hajj.
key_terms.حَجٌّ مُفْرَدٌ: Ifrad: A form of Hajj where one performs only Hajj without Umrah.
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of Hajj mentioned in Shia hadith and which one is preferred?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the three canonical forms of Hajj—Ifrad, Qiran, and Tamattu'—as the exclusive modes of pilgrimage commanded by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). It underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that these specific structures hold inherent virtue, thereby guiding the community to adhere strictly to these established methods rather than introducing novel practices. The narration highlights the continuity of prophetic authority in ritual law, affirming the validity of all three forms while emphasizing their divine origin.
